findings.reason: without one stated rule the §3 node either sends every below-floor single name to the lead, spending lead attention s5 deliberately refused, or silently departs from §3's routing, and neither outcome is reviewable.
findings.text: s5 now says "a single name below the floor keeps its stored domain, is counted, and is not sent to the lead", while §3 (plan.html:67) says "A family the decision reports undecided under the options §5 gives it ... is not left split unseen", and §2 (plan.html:53) defines "A name with no siblings is its own family", so the two rules give opposite instructions for the same name and a §3 node must break one of them

findings.reason: the gate can fail while the widened options work on every name they actually decided, or pass with the rise carried by a handful of names, so the node cannot tell which happened; recording the share over decided names beside the full draw makes the measure attributable.
findings.text: bullet 1 compares the share the decision files under the reader's domain against the share the stored domains reach, but s5's own rule leaves a below-floor single name at its stored domain, so those names contribute the stored share to both arms and the measured rise is diluted by an unrecorded count, and widening to 32 domains spreads the probability mass so this count grows rather than shrinks
